key_insight: WC–Co–Cr coating properties depend on powder morphology and spray method: detonation spraying delivers higher hardness, while HVOF yields a dense, uniform coating with low friction.
engineering_relevance: Selecting the powder and spray process can improve the wear resistance and durability of machine parts operating under intensive friction and high loads.
method: Compare WC–Co–Cr coatings deposited by detonation spraying and HVOF.
Examine powder morphology and coating microstructure using SEM and EDS.
Evaluate coating microhardness and tribological properties.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports average microhardness of 1449 HV for detonation-sprayed coatings and a friction coefficient of Kt = 0.143 for HVOF coatings.
watch_item: The abstract does not specify wear-test conditions, variability, or comparative wear rates, limiting confidence in service-life predictions.
paper_title: INVESTIGATION OF THE FORMATION OF STRUCTURE AND WEAR-RESISTANT PROPERTIES OF WC–CO–CR COATINGS PRODUCED BY HVOF AND DETONATION SPRAYING
